business_problem: Flix needed to stop spending engineering time on self-hosted Kafka so it could move travel data in real time, reduce latency into analytical stores, and accelerate product delivery for booking, fraud, and arrival use cases.
solution_summary: Flix moved its travel data platform to Confluent Cloud on AWS to modernize a self-hosted Kafka estate that had become too expensive and operationally heavy for a fast-growing travel business. The migration was executed in phases with Cluster Linking so existing systems could stay live while teams gradually moved over without downtime. Once in place, the platform used Flink for stream processing and managed connectors to push real-time data into Snowflake and Amazon S3, reducing downstream latency from batch-style 8 to 12 hour windows to near real time. Those governed streams support fraud detection, seat availability, ticket booking, arrival predictions, and a growing data mesh used by more than 50 internal teams. The same backbone also feeds AI-driven pricing and capacity systems that evaluate hundreds of millions of seat combinations and help Flix expand into new geographies faster.
